name: globe-cutaway
purpose: Dimensions used only to draw the cutaway globe around the optical surfaces (which come from the EyeParameters document). None of these affects any computed optical quantity.
citation: approximation; typical adult values pending transcription. Scleral thickness ~0.5 mm at the equator to ~1.0 mm posteriorly (Norman et al. 2010, Exp Eye Res 90:277); retinal thickness ~0.2-0.3 mm (OCT normative data); iris thickness ~0.4-0.6 mm; ora serrata ~6-8 mm behind the limbus; oraSerrataZMm is measured from the corneal vertex, which lies about 2 mm in front of the limbus plane, so the drawing uses 10.0 (8.0 previously placed it about 2 mm too far forward); scleral spur ~2 mm behind the limbus; ciliary body ~4-6 mm long (pars plicata + pars plana) and ~1-2 mm thick. The globe is drawn as the sphere of the retina radius, so the anterior segment is wider than a real eye; the ciliary body does not reach the lens equator here.
